title: King's Indian Defense: Fianchetto Variation
line: White's bishop guards its king from the long diagonal, so Black plays on the queen's side.

steps.text: Here White brings the knight out first and gets ready to put its own bishop on the long diagonal.
Castle. Your king is safe behind the bishop.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square, as in every King's Indian.
Bring the other knight out. It hits White's pawn on d4.
Move the pawn on a7 one square. The pawn on b7 can then push on, at White's pawn on c4.
steps.after: White pushes past and attacks your knight.

steps.text: Move the knight to the edge, where it attacks the pawn on c4.
steps.after: White's knight steps back to guard it.

steps.text: Push the pawn on c7 two squares. It takes space on the queen's side.
Put the rook behind the pawn on b7, to back up its push.
Now push that pawn two squares. It attacks the pawn on c4, and your rook and knight join in.

summary: Against White's bishop on the long diagonal, Black brings a knight, a rook and pawns to the queen's side.
